edit.description: Early same-clock historical forecasts, smoothly approach frozen static teachers
edit.interpolation: smoothstep; phase is normalized over observed score nodes; no extrapolation
edit.normalization: dose is normalized over actual score nodes to a mean of one

failure_modes: Affinity is primary but decoded final affinity is unobserved (recorded affinities removed, equal score prior), so no affinity improvement can be claimed from this evidence; the edit is justified only as a coordinate-shape control.

Component gradients of the observed-forecast and static terms may cancel, producing a near-zero combined endpoint VJP even though the scalar reward changes; distinguishing cancellation from an unsuitable target requires gradient-direction and delivered-dose checks, not scalar value alone.
A changing scalar reward does not prove changed injection: realized per-seed dose and trace changes must be audited, since equal sum(dt*w) is only a ratio budget under RMS normalization.

The observed-node linear fit was rejected (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE≈0.78) and only one feature was read, so the contrast is qualitative and may not generalize to other landmarks or held-out batches.
If first and last rate signs agree on a held-out batch set, or the whole-window mean is far from zero, the time-resolved contrast premise fails and the edit should be reverted to retain.
rationale: H001/H002 describe a non-monotone, level-neutral time-dependent contrast in landmark_00_local_dx over the observed score window [0.0,0.49], with opposite-sign endpoint rates and a near-zero whole-window mean. A reward that only targets the window-integrated level cannot represent this shape, so a time-resolved reward is warranted. S1_observed_to_static is the registered reward-route recipe that keeps dose_factors=1 and delta fixed while smoothly shifting teacher relevance from early same-clock historical forecasts toward frozen static teachers across the observed score nodes, matching the observed early-to-late contrast without extrapolation. S2_constant_blend and S3_static_to_observed_control are retained as the constant-blend and time-order controls needed to attribute any benefit to timing rather than to blending per se.
